question: Can an XRPL escrow hold RLUSD today, and what must the issuer enable before a buyer can lock it?

plan.restatement: Whether XRPL escrows can hold RLUSD today and what the issuer must enable before a buyer can lock it.
subqueries: XRPL escrow token escrow amendment issuer enable

requirements.text: Whether XRPL escrow can hold RLUSD today, with the date
What the RLUSD issuer must enable before a buyer can lock it in escrow
The XRPL amendment or feature governing token escrow for issued assets

lead: Not today: an XRPL escrow can hold official RLUSD only after its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking, and the RLUSD issuer had not enabled it on Mainnet or Testnet when the team checked on 11 November 2026.
conclusion: Not today: an XRPL escrow can hold official RLUSD only after its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking, and the RLUSD issuer had not enabled it on Mainnet or Testnet when the team checked on 11 November 2026. The TokenEscrow amendment (XLS-85), which lets an escrow hold issued tokens, is already enabled on both networks, so the issuer flag is the remaining blocker. Only the issuer can set that flag, with an AccountSet transaction; a buyer or writer cannot set it for them. An issuer can change its flags later, so check the issuer account on the intended network before relying on this answer.

question: How much XRP reserve does an agent wallet need, and how much does each open escrow or trust line add?

plan.restatement: The XRP reserve an agent wallet needs on the XRP Ledger, and how much each open escrow or trust line adds.
subqueries: XRPL owner reserve per object escrow trust line
XRPL reserve requirements escrow trust line cost

requirements.text: Current XRPL base account reserve in XRP, with date
Current XRPL owner reserve per object in XRP, with date
How much an open escrow adds to an agent wallet's XRP reserve
How much an open trust line adds to an agent wallet's XRP reserve

lead: An XRPL wallet needs a base reserve of 1 XRP plus an owner reserve of 0.2 XRP for each object it owns, such as an escrow, offer or trust line, at current Mainnet settings.
conclusion: An XRPL wallet needs a base reserve of 1 XRP plus an owner reserve of 0.2 XRP for each object it owns, such as an escrow, offer or trust line, at current Mainnet settings. The reserve is held separately from the money the wallet intends to send. Base reserve supports the account's existence; owner reserve constrains ledger objects. Removing an object can release its reserve requirement. Treating every XRP in a balance as transferable would therefore confuse several distinct accounting concepts. Reserves are not payments to validators, and the documentation permits reserved XRP to pay transaction costs.
